document.title: Weekly South Asia Activity Report
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Weekly report on South Asia developments: Afghan refugees fleeing Kabul, the UN Mestiri mission, and the stranded Pakistani convoy. It mentions the debriefing of British kidnapping victims who identified their captor as "Rohit Sharma", i.e. Ahmed Omar Saeed Sheikh, later the self-confessed mastermind of the Daniel Pearl kidnapping.

events.description: American Bella Nuss kidnapped by Kashmiri militants found in Ghaziabad
Babar and Western envoys visited Herat and Kandahar
Shariat activists in Malakand killed a provincial minister and occupied police stations and Swat airport
Fighting in Kandahar between Taliban and HIG/NIFA commanders over Chaman-Kandahar highway and Spin Boldak
Shariat activists killed a provincial minister, occupied police stations and Swat airport, and barricaded government offices; government dispatched 8,000 troops.
Assassination of UNP candidate Gamini Dissanayake.
Two hostages held in Kashmir by kidnappers who claimed to be same as those holding British victims.

Kashmiri militant group (reportedly with Afghan connections) abducted an American and threatened to kill him and three Britons unless 10 militants were released; Nuss was found in chains in Ghaziabad.
Russian Deputy FM Chernyshev and Pakistani FM Ali discussed PM Bhutto's visit to Russia and Kashmir while in Islamabad for Tajik talks.
Northern Areas Council elections: Shia TJP won 8 of 25 seats, PPP 6, PML/N 1.
Interior Minister Babar and Western envoys including Ambassador Monjo visited Herat and made a short stop in Kandahar.
Bombing in Sri Lanka killed UNP presidential candidate Gamini Dissanayake.
State funeral for Gamini Dissanayake took place peacefully.
Agreement reached to restructure and resume the McCollum program of DOD humanitarian supplies to Afghanistan, including aid for Afghans fleeing Kabul for Jalalabad.
Tajik government and opposition negotiators in Islamabad agreed to extend the Afghan-Tajik border cease-fire until February 1995; cease-fire began October 20.
Opposition deputies walked out of the National Assembly on Oct 29 and 30 after the GOP refused to allow three jailed opposition members to participate; Speaker Gilani ordered their attendance.
Two Massoud pilots reportedly defected to Dostum.
Fighting erupted in Kandahar province between Taliban and HIG/NIFA commanders over Chaman-Kandahar highway.
Shariat activists killed a provincial minister, occupied police stations and an airport in Swat, barricaded government offices.
Government dispatched 8,000 troops to Malakand Division.
UNP candidate Dissanayake assassinated.
Two hostages held in Kashmir by kidnappers who claimed to be the same as those holding three Britons.
Agreement reached to restructure and resume the McCollum humanitarian supply program for Afghanistan.
Tajik government and opposition negotiators in Islamabad agreed to extend the Afghan-Tajik border cease-fire until February 1995.
Opposition deputies walked out of National Assembly sessions on Oct 29 and 30 over jailed opposition members.
About a thousand IDPs per day arrive in Jalalabad from Kabul; UNOCHA anticipates 150,000 new arrivals.
Mestiri began discussions on an interim ruling council after meetings with Rabbani, Hekmatyar, Ismail Khan, Masood, Dostam.
Pakistani and Indian delegates clashed over Kashmir at the UN General Assembly.
Foreign Secretary Shaikh met Ambassador Monjo on Kashmir and nonproliferation.
PM Bhutto spoke at ceremony in Karachi for business women.
Two Masood pilots reportedly defected to Dostam.
Clash in Kandahar province between four local commanders and the Taliban over a test-case Pakistani convoy to Central Asia.

key_claims: The Taliban emerged in early November 1994 as a new, well-armed group of religious students fighting HIG and NIFA commanders in Kandahar.
The Taliban's immediate goal appeared to be reopening the Chaman-Kandahar highway.
Many suspected the Taliban were backed by the Government of Pakistan and business interests seeking trade routes to Central Asia.
The Taliban's clash united normally rival Kandahar commanders.
Mestiri's interim council initiative was opposed by Sayyaf, Khalis, and Mohammadi.
Hekmatyar's blockade prevented UN and ICRC food deliveries to Kabul.
Shariat activists in Malakand Division escalated violence in early November 1994, killing a provincial minister and occupying Swat airport.
Pakistan deployed 8,000 troops to restore order in Malakand.
Pakistan's refugee plan was expected to rely on incentives rather than forced returns.
British kidnappers in New Delhi claimed links to the June Kashmir hostage-takers.
